grades.quote: demonstrate a program continuing to make use of an open file after all names for that file have been removed.
grades.reason: Exercise 8.10 asks the reader to demonstrate a program still using an open file after all its names are removed. That is the same phenomenon, but the passage only assigns a task and gives no explanation of why it happens.

grades.quote: iput() doesn’t truncate a file immediately when the link count for the file drops to zero, because some process might still hold a reference to the inode in memory: a process might still be reading and writing to the file, because
grades.reason: Explains directly that when the link count reaches zero the file isn't truncated at once, because a process that already opened it may still hold a reference and keep reading and writing it.

grades.quote: The unlink system call removes a name from the file system. The file’s inode and the disk space holding its content are only freed when the file’s link count is zero and no file descriptors refer to it.
grades.reason: Explains that unlink only removes a name. The inode and content are freed only when the link count is zero and no file descriptors refer to it, so the file stays accessible through another link or an open descriptor.
